title: Star Cluster Bursts into Life in New Hubble Image
caption: The young star cluster in the nebula NGC 3603, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 3603 · constellation Carina · about 20,000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage (STScI/AURA)-ESA/Hubble Collaboration; Acknowledgment: J. Maíz Apellániz (Institute of Astrophysics of Andalucía, Spain)

recognition.text: NASA Hubble image release (STScI). No published audience rating.

story: Thousands of young stars crowd the middle of a giant nebula, surrounded by a broad region of gas and dust. The nebula is NGC 3603, a prominent stellar nursery about 20,000 light-years away in our galaxy's Carina spiral arm, and its central cluster ranks among the most massive young clusters in the Milky Way.

The bluest and hottest stars have blown a large bubble around the cluster with their ultraviolet radiation and fast winds. Pushing outward, that flood of energy carved tall, dark stalks of dense gas into the nebula's walls. These columns stand a few light-years high, point back toward the cluster, and may be places where new stars are forming.

Near the top right corner sits a group of small dark clouds called Bok globules. Each is made of dense dust and gas holding about 10 to 50 times the mass of the Sun, and each may be collapsing under its own gravity on the way to forming stars. The scene spans roughly 17 light-years.

understand.summary: Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys took the image through three broad filters, with F435W shown in blue, F550M in green and the near-infrared F850LP in red.
understand.eye: The red channel records near-infrared light that the eye cannot see, so the colors are a translation rather than a direct view.

explore: Sir John Herschel was the first to discover the nebula. The cluster, the stalks and the globules show several stages in the life of stars, from dark clouds that may still be collapsing to hot, massive stars that have already cleared space around themselves.

alt: A dense cluster of young stars inside a large bubble in a nebula, with tall dark stalks of gas and a group of small dark clouds near the top right.
